summary: Retirement is well-documented for a human reading the docs/INDEX/ADR. The chief ergonomic gap is the runtime path: an oncall who literally runs `cargo run -p oya-governance-archive-orphan-app` after this merge receives a generic cargo `package ID specification ... did not match any packages` error with no breadcrumb to ADR-0118.

oncall_useful_error_pointing_to_adr_0118.evidence: PR removes the entire crate + tools dir + workspace member. After merge `cargo run -p oya-governance-archive-orphan-app` produces cargo's default 'no matching package' error. No stub Cargo.toml, no tombstone main.rs, no CHANGELOG entry indexed by binary name. The only discoverability path is grepping `archive-orphan` in docs/, which an oncall under pressure may not do.
oncall_useful_error_pointing_to_adr_0118.suggested_fix: Either (a) leave a tiny tombstone tools/oya-governance-archive-orphan-app/src/main.rs whose only behavior is `eprintln!` pointing to ADR-0118 and exit 2, or (b) add an entry in docs/runbooks/retired-commands.md (create if absent) so `rg archive-orphan-app` lands on a one-screen explanation.

index_md_retired_status_obvious.evidence: docs/fitness-lanes/INDEX.md row now reads `archive-orphan | retired | ADR-0118 / ADR-0116 / M01-P18 replacement | retired | retired | retired; no CI invocation | 0 | retired`. The word `retired` is repeated in every cell and severity column, which is unambiguous. CHANGELOG row at the bottom dated 2026-05-16 explains why.
index_md_retired_status_obvious.minor_nit: The 64-lane total in the trailing paragraph is now stale; arithmetic still says 64 but one lane is dead. Either tag the row as `(retired, 63 active)` or update the count line.

adr_0118_explains_what_now.evidence: ADR-0118 clearly states the lane is retired and points at M01-P18 / projected-merge-state / conflict-kernel as the replacement substrate. It does NOT, however, give a future debugger a recipe for `what do I do if I find a Bominal-style orphan archive in 2026-Q3?`. The Decision section enumerates what was removed; the Rejected-alternatives section is good. A short `## What to do if you hit the original failure mode` paragraph would close the loop.
adr_0118_explains_what_now.suggested_fix: Add 2-3 sentences mapping the historical failure modes (archive copy missing, original still active, living code references archived path) to the M01-P18 admission/conflict kernels that now own those invariants by name, so future grep on `archive orphan` lands on a forwarding pointer rather than only an ADR title.

ip_008_evidence_self_explanatory.evidence: evidence/agentic-pipeline/ip-008-archive-glue.json adds a top-level `retirement` block with `retired_on`, `retired_by` (ADR path), `replacement` (M01-P18 / ADR-0116), `removed_workspace_members`, and `removed_archive_payload`. The `naming_justification` inside that block explicitly calls out the use of `removed_*` keys to distinguish deleted vs active artifacts. A future debugger opening only this JSON gets the full retirement story without having to cross-reference.
ip_008_evidence_self_explanatory.minor_nit: Top-level `status` is not updated to e.g. `retired`; only the appended `retirement` object signals it. A future automated reader keying on `status` will still see the original value.

additional_observations: IP-008 markdown plan was renamed from `Symbols-to-grit-claim` to `Retired-symbols` and from `Acceptance-test-commands` to `Retirement-validation-commands` — that delta is ergonomically excellent because the section headers themselves tell a reader the document is now historical.
ADR-0104 and ADR-0107 amendments are small and consistent (mark archive-orphan retired, redirect to authoritative-tracked / no-importer kernels). Surprise-minimization: high.
Cargo.lock and Cargo.toml workspace members are both purged in the same commit — no half-state for `cargo metadata`.
registry/catalog deletions (3 yamls) are clean; no orphan capability entries left.

non_blocking_findings.finding: Running the retired binary by package name yields a generic cargo error with no pointer to ADR-0118.
non_blocking_findings.fix: Tombstone main.rs OR a retired-commands runbook indexed by binary name.

non_blocking_findings.finding: docs/fitness-lanes/INDEX.md trailing `Total: 64 lanes` no longer matches the de-facto active count.
non_blocking_findings.fix: Change to `Total: 64 lanes (1 retired -> 63 active)` or similar.

non_blocking_findings.finding: ADR-0118 lacks an explicit `what to do if you hit the original failure mode` forwarding paragraph.
non_blocking_findings.fix: Add 2-3 sentences naming the M01-P18 kernel that now owns each historical failure mode.

non_blocking_findings.finding: Top-level `status` field in ip-008-archive-glue.json (n/a - file has no top-level status, only embedded retirement block) — automated readers keyed on a status field will not see retirement.
non_blocking_findings.fix: Add top-level `lifecycle_status: retired` mirroring the embedded block.

verdict_rationale: All four judgment criteria pass on the documentation surface (INDEX, ADR, lane spec, evidence JSON). The single ergonomic regression is at the CLI surface: a deleted package name is the unfriendliest possible error message for an oncall in a hurry. That is fixable in a 5-line follow-up and is not a blocker for an already-merged PR.
